design_assessment: Three concentric perimeters: (a) global middleware enforces TrustHosts anchoring (regex `^127\.0\.0\.1$` blocks `127X0X0X1` bypass + Wave 2c heal) and TrustProxies=* for per-IP throttle keying (Wave 3 P1 heal); (b) api middleware group enforces throttle:api (default limiter from config app.api_throttle_per_minute) + JSON normalization + correlation-id propagation + EnsureUserStatusActive per-request token revocation gate (Sprint H1 Z6-06); (c) per-prefix middleware stacks layer auth:sanctum + apiKey + named throttle (admin-mutation, pos-quote, pos-order-create, pos-order-update, kiosk-orders, oss-public, etc.) + opt-in `idempotency` middleware on financially-sensitive POSTs. Middleware composition pattern is `installed → apiKey → auth:sanctum → localization → throttle:<bucket>` repeated 5 times for /api/admin (split groups for separate throttle buckets) + /api/frontend + /api/table + /api/profile + /api/auth. Per-IP key derivation works because TrustProxies passes through X-Forwarded-For from the local nginx fronting PHP-FPM.

middleware_ordering_assessment.evidence: Kernel.php:85-97 defines local $middlewarePriority array that explicitly places EnsureUserStatusActive AFTER AuthenticatesRequests. Without this override, Foundation\Http\Kernel::sortMiddleware() would array_unshift EnsureUserStatusActive to position 0 (line 410 of the vendor parent), running it BEFORE Sanctum resolves the user, causing every authenticated request to short-circuit with `if (! $user)` passthrough at EnsureUserStatusActive.php:51-53 — i.e., the gate would silently no-op. The local override is the load-bearing piece. Verified post-113-commit drift: the array is still in place, line range unchanged, no removal commits in `git log --all -- app/Http/Kernel.php`.
middleware_ordering_assessment.regression_risk: P3 — sentinel coverage. No automated test asserts the priority array exists. If a future refactor strips it (e.g., aligning back to vanilla Laravel Kernel), the gate silently degrades. RECOMMEND adding a sentinel: `tests/Feature/Sentinels/MiddlewarePrioritySentinelTest.php` asserting `(new Kernel(...))->middlewarePriority` contains EnsureUserStatusActive immediately after AuthenticatesRequests.

architecture_concerns.finding: Two sibling /api/admin route groups (L256 + L270) use DIFFERENT throttle buckets (60,1 vs admin-mutation). This is a documented anti-pattern from BLUE 2026-05-08 B3-S5 — needed to avoid POS cashier 429 self-DoS at rush hour. The siblings ARE NOT NESTED (which would stack to min(30,60)=30). Both share the same `installed,apiKey,auth:sanctum,localization` 4-tuple prefix. Future readers may not realize the split is intentional and merge them in a refactor; sentinel coverage absent.
architecture_concerns.remediation: Add a comment-anchor sentinel: a `tests/Feature/Sentinels/AvailabilityToggleSeparateThrottleSentinelTest.php` EXISTS (verified). It locks /menu/availability/* throttle bucket to NOT be admin-mutation. Defense-in-depth coverage already in place. Closing as documented.

architecture_concerns.finding: Closure-based POS counter-collect routes (api.php L769-839) are 70+ LOC inline closures with try/catch + abort_unless auth checks. Should be controller methods on a dedicated CounterCollectController. Inline closures bypass `routes:cache` optimization (Laravel docs: closures cannot be route-cached) and make middleware composition harder to read. Pre-prod observed: 5 closure routes × ~15 LOC = 75 LOC inline; if route-cache is needed for cold-start latency (prod queue worker boot), these closures will silently disable artisan route:cache.
architecture_concerns.remediation: V1.0.2 — extract to App\Http\Controllers\Admin\Pos\CounterCollectController. Authorize via __construct middleware `permission:pos`. Zero behavior change. Sentinel: assert RouteCollection contains no closure-target POST routes (count baseline = current 5).

architecture_concerns.finding: FormRequest authz coverage is incomplete by V1 design — 66/97 FormRequest classes still have naked `return true;` in authorize() (sentinel baseline = 69, actual = 66, drift sentinel emits diagnostic since count shrunk). The hot endpoints have been progressively healed (Wave 5H = 5, BUILD-6 = 8, AdministratorRequest, PosLoyaltyRedeemRequest). Remaining ~66 are gated by their route middleware (`permission:settings`, etc.) but if a route is ever wired to those FormRequests without a `permission:*` gate, the FormRequest will admit unauthenticated access. Effective today: route gate is the load-bearing piece for those 66.

app/Http/Requests/AnalyticSectionRequest.php (relevant — route lacks permission gate, see WI-4-S-01)

New refactors should target highest-blast first: MenuTemplateRequest, AnalyticSectionRequest, KioskSetupRequest, LoyaltySetupRequest, OrderSetupRequest, MailRequest (settings family).

architecture_concerns.finding: Closure-defined inline GET /api/admin/pos/counter-collect/pending (L769-784) executes a complex Eloquent query with branch isolation logic INSIDE the route closure. Branch resolution `$branchId = (int) (auth()->user()?->branch_id ?? 0); if ($branchId > 0) { $query->where('branch_id', $branchId); }` is duplicated logic that exists in BranchScope global scope — should rely on the global scope rather than re-implement. Today: when admin/Tenant Admin (branch_id=0) calls this, BranchScope applies its own bypass (admin@0 cross-branch), but the in-closure logic short-circuits the where-clause, achieving the same effect by accident. Code duplication = drift risk.
architecture_concerns.remediation: Extract to controller method. Use Order::query() (which auto-applies BranchScope) + remove the manual branch_id where-clause. Sentinel: assert results equivalent for admin@0 + staff@N before and after.

architecture_concerns.finding: Frontend kiosk routes (api.php L1191-1364) duplicate `auth:sanctum + throttle:kiosk-orders + idempotency` triplet on /order POST + similar combos on /pricing/preview + /promo/validate + /upsell + /loyalty/* + /kiosk/event. ~12 routes each redeclare similar 2-3-tuple middleware. A `Route::middleware(['auth:sanctum', 'kiosk.locale'])->group(function() {...})` wrapper would tidy. Cosmetic — no security impact.

Health endpoints (/health, /health/live, /health/ready at L139-141) have NO middleware whatsoever — not even throttle:api. A malicious unauthenticated caller can hammer /health/ready (which performs a real DB SELECT + Redis PING + storage check per HealthController). At 1k req/sec, this saturates the DB connection pool. P3 because production fronting will typically reject from k8s liveness IP allowlist or ingress rate limit before hitting Laravel. Defense-in-depth: add throttle:60,1.
architecture_concerns.remediation: Add `->middleware('throttle:60,1')` to /health/full and /health/ready (NOT /health/live which must be a fast in-memory PHP no-op for k8s).
